import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set a visually appealing style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a box plot to visualize the distribution of camera prices
# broken down by 'body_type' and further categorized by 'sensor_type'.
# This helps understand how these key specifications influence pricing.
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8)) # Adjust figure size for better readability and legend placement
sns.boxplot(
    data=df,
    x='body_type',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    palette='viridis', # Use a distinct color palette
    linewidth=1.0,
    fliersize=3 # Adjust size of outlier points
)

# Add a descriptive title to the plot
plt.title('Camera Price Distribution by Body Type and Sensor Type', fontsize=16, pad=20)

# Label the axes clearly
plt.xlabel('Body Type', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)

# Place the legend outside the plot area to prevent overlap with data points
plt.legend(title='Sensor Type', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Adjust layout to ensure all elements (especially the legend) fit within the figure
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
